question.worked_solution:
Notice that the given expression is a sum of squares, since

$$
{x}^{12}+81={({x}^{6})}^{2}+{9}^{2}.
$$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${i}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{12}+81 & ={x}^{12}-(-81) \\  & ={x}^{12}-(81{i}^{2}) \\  & ={({x}^{6})}^{2}-(9i)^{2} \\  & =({x}^{6}+9i)({x}^{6}-9i)\end{aligned}
$$
